answer: Persistent Compute Ledger. Each identity must continuously publish verifiable compute receipts from a unique hardware root; agents earn routing priority only while their ledger stays live. Cloning forces the attacker to run fresh hardware at the mesa of full power draw, and idle clones fall to a nadir of zero visibility. The rule: one live ledger, one identity. A clone needs its own sustained compute, so every extra identity costs a full machine's electricity plus the ember of reputation it must rebuild from scratch.
